purpose: Document city-scope registry evidence and bounded public parcel-geometry route review.
assessment: The City-hosted Title Parcels layer provides a plausible public polygon-source candidate, but the bounded safe-field query returned 403, so no feature geometry or exact locator coverage is verified. The City states polygon parcel open-data products were retired in 2021; the existence of this viewer sublayer alone does not establish redistribution rights.
registryAssessment: Municipal-boundary title/cadastral mapping is identified by the City as maintained/distributed through ADP and AltaLIS. The City-hosted public viewer has Title Parcels and Legal Parcels sublayers; this does not establish an unrestricted downloadable geometry license.

officialPrimarySources.observation: The City states that ADP and AltaLIS maintain/distribute cadastral and title mapping for parcels within Edmonton municipal boundaries.
City notice says polygon parcel open-data datasets were retired from its catalog in 2021; replacement open-data layers are centroids only.

Current ArcGIS child layer metadata identifies Title Parcels as a polygon layer, native OBJECTID, EPSG:3776 source reference, EPSG:3857 metadata extent, and JSON/GeoJSON query formats. Schema includes address and other descriptive fields; only OBJECTID and geometry were selected in the attempted safe query.
Official public SLIM map provides legal-description, zoning, and assessment lookup tools; the city-hosted Property Lines group includes Title Parcels and Legal Parcels sublayers.
City describes distribution of mapping products through its open-data portal, Map Desk, and Alberta Data Partnerships.
